The U.S. stock market ended the month on a rather sour note, with both the S&P; 500 and the NASDAQ closing February in the red, while the Dow managed to just edge into the black.
After a strong start in January, the tech rally cooled, as investors grew concerned about market concentration.
Tech stocks tumbled, while defensive and cyclical stocks trended higher.
Mega-cap stocks, which carried the market throughout 2025, saw increased volatility in 2026.
Investors questioned big-tech valuations, seizing an opportunity to take profits.
In February, money moved to value stocks, such as energy, materials, and consumer staples.
While January was a strong month for the U.S. economy, February presented a more complex picture.
The labor market stabilized somewhat, while new trade policies and fiscal shifts created volatility in the markets.
Gross domestic product appears to be in a recovery phase following last year's government shutdown.
Economic growth slowed from 4.4% in the third quarter of 2025 to 1.4% in the fourth quarter.
Consumer spending grew by 2.4% in the fourth quarter vs. an expansion of 3.5% in the previous quarter and 3.9% from a year earlier.
Price pressures continued to moderate but remained above the Federal Reserve's 2.0% target, impacted by tariffs, both threatened and realized, and overall fiscal policy uncertainty.
The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, a preferred measure of inflation by the Federal Reserve, rose 0.4% in December (+0.2% in November) and 2.9% from December 2024 (+2.8% for the 12 months ended in November 2025).
...
Job growth, which had slowed considerably, rose from 48,000 in December to 130,000 in January.
...
The Federal Reserve did not meet in February but held interest rates steady in January.
While inflation slowly drew nearer to its 2.0% target, the Fed's stance suggests they are waiting to see how new trade policies impact price stability before considering further cuts.
Among the market sectors, energy, utilities, consumer staples, and industrials led the way, while consumer discretionary and information technology each fell more than 7.0%.
...
While investors move into March looking for economic improvement and a slowdown in price pressures, the recent escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East will likely increase short-term uncertainty.

results.snippet:
The S&P 500 fell 6.8% in March 2026, its worst monthly decline since December 2022.
The Dow tumbled nearly 800 points in a single session on March 26, officially entering correction territory.
...
Three forces converged to create the selloff.
First, the Strait of Hormuz crisis sent oil prices from $67 to over $110 per barrel, raising the specter of 1970s-style stagflation.
Second, the Supreme Court's tariff ruling created trade policy chaos -- tariffs remain but on shaky legal ground, with a 150-day expiration clock ticking.
Third, the Iran war itself introduced geopolitical uncertainty that markets despise.
The numbers tell the story.
Import prices rose 1.3% in February alone, the highest since March 2022, with fuel prices up 3.8%.
Goldman Sachs estimated that 67% of tariff costs will fall on consumers by mid-2026.
Moody's chief economist Mark Zandi warned that the combination of oil shocks and tariffs could push the economy into recession.
...
US stock markets entered 2026 at record highs, with the S&P 500 peaking at 6,797 in January.
The decline began in late February as the Iran conflict erupted, accelerated through the Supreme Court tariff ruling, and deepened as the Strait of Hormuz closure drove oil prices to multi-year highs.
By late March, the S&P 500 had posted five consecutive losing weeks.
...

Why is the stock market falling in March 2026?
Three simultaneous shocks are driving the decline: the Strait of Hormuz oil crisis (oil jumped from $67 to $126/barrel), trade policy chaos after the Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs, and geopolitical uncertainty from the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.
Each alone would pressure markets; together they have created the worst monthly decline since late 2022.

{"figures":[{"fact_key":"Start date","value":"2025-09-10"},{"fact_key":"End date","value":"2026-09-09"},{"fact_key":"Starting capital","value":1000},{"fact_key":"Total money contributed","value":1000},{"fact_key":"Purchases and sales","value":4},{"fact_key":"Worst drop began","value":"2025-12-05"},{"fact_key":"Worst drop ended","value":"2026-03-30"},{"fact_key":"Portfolio value before the worst drop","value":1039},{"fact_key":"Portfolio value at the bottom of the worst drop","value":988},{"fact_key":"Worst drop from a prior high","value":4.8},{"fact_key":"Ending portfolio value","value":1086},{"fact_key":"Highest portfolio value","value":1086},{"fact_key":"Total return on starting capital","value":8.6},{"fact_key":"Benchmark return","value":16.9},{"fact_key":"Return difference versus benchmark","value":8.3},{"fact_key":"Annualized volatility","value":6.1},{"fact_key":"Sharpe ratio","value":1.4}],"language":"es-419","text":"Entre el 10 de septiembre de 2025 y el 9 de septiembre de 2026, la estrategia trabajó con una sola aportación inicial de $1,000. No fue simplemente comprar SPY y mantenerlo: las señales de umbral RSI llevaron a 4 compras y ventas durante el periodo. En otras palabras, mantener esta estrategia implicó entrar y salir de SPY en distintos momentos, en vez de permanecer expuesto todo el tiempo.

El entorno empezó siendo favorable para las acciones estadounidenses. Al inicio del periodo, el S&P 500 marcaba nuevos máximos mientras los inversionistas esperaban recortes de tasas de la Reserva Federal, según [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/wall-street-indexes-notch-record-high-closes-investors-bet-rate-cut-2025-09-09/). Después llegaron más sobresaltos: preocupaciones por la concentración y las valuaciones de las grandes empresas tecnológicas, nuevas políticas comerciales, inflación todavía elevada y dudas sobre el crecimiento. Un resumen de mercado de marzo describió precisamente ese cambio, con una rotación desde tecnología hacia sectores más defensivos y cíclicos, además de incertidumbre por aranceles y política fiscal ([Camden National Bank](https://www.camdennational.bank/wealth/market-briefs/market-brief-march-2026)).

La parte más difícil para esta cartera ocurrió del 5 de diciembre de 2025 al 30 de marzo de 2026. Desde un máximo de $1,039 bajó a $988, una caída de 4.8%. Eso representa una pérdida de $51 desde ese máximo antes de la recuperación. Las noticias de ese tramo apuntaron a una combinación de tensión geopolítica, petróleo más caro, expectativas de tasas altas y temor a una desaceleración económica. Associated Press reportó que el S&P 500 cerró el 30 de marzo en un nuevo mínimo del año mientras el petróleo superaba $100 y la incertidumbre sobre el conflicto con Irán pesaba sobre el mercado ([AP vía WTOP](https://wtop.com/world/2026/03/how-major-stock-indexes-fared-monday-3-30-2026/)).

Luego el mercado se recuperó. Para el final de la prueba, el valor llegó a $1,086, que también fue el máximo de la cartera. En total, la estrategia ganó 8.6% sobre los $1,000 iniciales. El resultado fue relativamente menos brusco que una cartera con movimientos más amplios, con una volatilidad anualizada de 6.1% y un Sharpe de 1.4, aunque esas medidas no describen por sí solas cómo se sintió cada día.

La comparación importante es que el benchmark, también basado en SPY, ganó 16.9%. La estrategia quedó 8.3 pp por debajo. La lectura más directa es que las entradas y salidas protegieron parte del recorrido durante los periodos difíciles, pero también dejaron pasar parte de la subida de SPY, especialmente porque el mercado terminó recuperándose después del mínimo de marzo. Así, la experiencia fue positiva en dinero al final, pero con un costo claro frente a simplemente mantener el benchmark: se terminó con $1,086 en vez de aproximadamente $1,169 sobre la misma base inicial."}
